saying: Nearly all commenters accept outside contributions to postmarket monitoring only if roles are split by distinct function, with manufacturers keeping the monitoring program, complaint handling, aggregation, and corrective action. Many ask FDA to specify what manufacturers must supply institutions—version identifiers, logs, notice of model changes—and to name omitted actors such as clinical engineering staff, payers, and patients.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on how much monitoring work deploying institutions should do: one says institutions should only inventory functions, retain manufacturer logs, and report failures, not evaluate independently, because capacity varies; others assign institutions local validation, workflow and protocol monitoring, and defined reporting pathways.

sides.summary: Institutional role should be limited to inventory, log retention, and reporting; evaluation burden belongs with manufacturers.
Institutions should actively monitor locally, including local validation, workflow and protocol changes, and owned reporting pathways.
